Maya (Design): posted a GIF of the run history where function calls are collapsed into a single summary line — demo: https://figma.com/file/abc/playground-run-history (preview) Maya (Design): main concern: users can't discover the structured output behind a collapsed call. the summary "Table extracted" is ambiguous. Leo (DevEx): saw a user file a bug that they couldn't find the CSV payload after a run. we should make the collapsed state show a tiny badge (icon + type) and a disclosure chevron. Priya (Frontend): small perf note: adding many badges in a long run history can blow up the render. can we lazily hydrate badges when the row enters viewport? Noah (Eng-ML): also consider the streaming case: tool emits partial rows, we need skeletons in expanded view not in the summary. otherwise summary flickers while streaming. Jules (QA): accessibility check: when row expands, keyboard focus should move into the first interactive element inside the expanded panel, not remain on the summary button. otherwise keyboard users lose context. A11y-bot: automatch: suggested aria pattern: summary button gets aria-expanded, expanded panel gets role="region" aria-label="Run history details for call at 1748001234" and focus trap avoided. Maya (Design): copy tweak: change "Table extracted" -> "Tool: excel_extract — table (3 rows)". shorter but more explicit. show friendly tool name + result type + quick count. Leo (DevEx): love the count. telemetry: capture expand/collapse and copy actions: events `run_history_expand`, `run_history_copy_payload`. add small cooldown so we don't flood analytics on streaming. Priya (Frontend): mock markup I'm proposing: ```html 
{...}
``` Priya (Frontend): plan: virtualize rows, hydrate details on open. ETA 3 days. Noah (Eng-ML): minor UX idea: show a tiny schema hint inline next to the badge like `↑schema: rows[cols]` so users scanning history can spot structured outputs without expanding. e.g., "rows[3] cols[6]" Maya (Design): that inline schema hint is interesting but avoid noise. maybe a tooltip on hover for the badge with `rows × cols` and a short preview. Jules (QA): test cases I'll add: keyboard expand/collapse, screen reader readout order (summary -> label -> payload), streaming partial payload behavior (no duplicate announcements). A11y-bot: accessibility checklist: 1) summary button has aria-controls to the details id, 2) aria-expanded toggles, 3) details panel role=region with descriptive aria-label, 4) copy button focusable and announced as "Copy payload". Leo (DevEx): copy UX nit: when user clicks copy on a large JSON, show a transient toast "Payload copied" and include a small inline action "Open" which also toggles the details. avoids extra clicks. Priya (Frontend): implementation detail: Copy uses navigator.clipboard.writeText; for big payloads we should stream copy to avoid blocking main thread. fallback to hidden textarea for older browsers. Maya (Design): for run history filters (by tool, type, time) let's add a compact pill bar above the list. copy text: "Filter: Tools, Types, Time" -> propose "Filter results" to be concise. Noah (Eng-ML): back-compat: some runs are from older function defs and include no structured metadata; show "legacy" badge in gray to set expectations. Jules (QA): I'll validate legacy badge + tooltip text. also test mobile narrow widths (wrap behavior). Maya (Design): small copy proposals in-line: - summary placeholder: "Tool: excel_extract — table (3 rows)" - expand button aria: "Show details for excel_extract output" - badge tooltip: "Schema: rows × cols" Which phrasing do we prefer? short vs explicit? :thinking_face: Leo (DevEx): prefer explicit in summary, short in badge. telemetry: also record whether users use filters vs search. Priya (Frontend): I'll push the feature branch to `devex/run-history-inline` and attach PR when ready. A11y-bot: note: ensure any dynamically injected aria-live announcements are rate-limited and only describe significant state changes. Maya (Design): quick poll: react with :thumbsup: if you like explicit summary text, :eyes: if you prefer very compact text (just tool + type). Maya (Design): :thumbsup: from Maya Priya (Frontend): :thumbsup: Noah (Eng-ML): :eyes: (lean compact for dense histories) Jules (QA): :thumbsup: Leo (DevEx): :thumbsup: Maya (Design): thanks! will land mocks + test script later today and ping QA.
